findings.lesson_title: Challenges for Religion in a Secular Society
findings.claim: The Monarch is the Supreme Governor of the Church of England, a role that dates to Henry VIII's break with Rome in 1534.
findings.issue: Henry VIII's 1534 Act of Supremacy created the title 'Supreme Head of the Church of England', not 'Supreme Governor'. The title 'Supreme Governor' was introduced by Elizabeth I's 1559 Act of Supremacy. Attributing 'Supreme Governor' to Henry VIII / 1534 is factually wrong — a well-tested distinction at GCSE and A-level.
findings.correction: The Monarch is the Supreme Governor of the Church of England — a title created by Elizabeth I's Act of Supremacy (1559). Henry VIII's 1534 Act had made him 'Supreme Head'. Elizabeth's advisers adopted 'Governor' partly to deflect criticism that a woman could not be head of the church.
findings.source: Wikipedia — Supreme Governor of the Church of England; Acts of Supremacy (1534 and 1559)
